title: Stale incomplete digest records can permanently suppress catch-up for the day

evidence.quote: let digest = Digest(... isComplete: false, ... period: period) ... try await digestRepository.createDigest(digest)
digest.isComplete = false; digest.errorMessage = error.localizedDescription; try await digestRepository.updateDigest(digest)

reasoning: DigestGenerator creates and saves an incomplete digest with nil error before doing network and EPUB work. If the process is killed, crashes, or is terminated during background expiration before the catch block updates errorMessage, that record remains incomplete with nil error. The catch-up helper treats any incomplete nil-error digest for the period as covering the latest period, so foreground catch-up can skip generation for the rest of the day even though no usable digest exists.
reproduction: Start scheduled generation for MORNING, let createDigest persist the initial isComplete=false record, then terminate the app before updateDigest runs. Reopen after the morning time; checkForMissedDigests loads today's digests, hasDigestCoveringLatestPeriod returns true for the stale in-progress record, and no replacement digest is generated.
recommendation: Do not let stale persisted in-progress records satisfy catch-up indefinitely. Count incomplete nil-error digests only when they are known to correspond to an active in-memory generation, or add an age threshold and mark/ignore stale in-progress records before deciding coverage.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: LocalDigestSchedulerTests verify that failed digests with an error are ignored, but there is no case for an incomplete nil-error digest older than the active generation window. DigestGeneratorTests only verify unique filenames across successful runs.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a scheduler helper test with an incomplete digest for the latest period, nil errorMessage, and generatedAt sufficiently in the past; assert it does not cover the period and catch-up would attempt generation.
minimumFixScope: LocalDigestScheduler.hasDigestCoveringLatestPeriod plus a small stale-in-progress policy; optionally add repository cleanup/mark-failed behavior on startup.
